verses.text: This is the message that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Listen to the terms of this covenant, and tell them to the people of Judah and to those who live in Jerusalem.
Tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Cursed is anyone who does not obey the terms of this covenant,
the terms I commanded your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, "Obey me and do everything I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God.
Then I will keep the promise I made to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey," the land you live in today.'" I answered, "Amen, LORD. Let it be so."
The LORD said to me, "Announce all these words in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: 'Listen to the terms of this covenant and obey them.
From the time I brought your ancestors out of Egypt until today, I have warned them again and again, saying, "Obey me."

But they did not listen or pay attention. Each of them followed their own stubborn, evil heart. So I brought on them all the punishments written in this covenant, which I had commanded them to obey but they did not.'"
Then the LORD said to me, "There is a plot among the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the sins of their ancestors, who refused to listen to my words. They have followed other gods to serve them. Both Israel and Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.
So this is what the LORD says: 'Look, I will bring a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the people of the towns of Judah and Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn incense to, but those gods will not save them at all when disaster strikes.
Judah, you have as many gods as you have towns. And you have set up as many altars to burn incense to that shameful god Baal as there are streets in Jerusalem.'
So do not pray for these people, Jeremiah. Do not cry out or pray for them, because I will not listen when they call to me in their time of trouble.
What right does my beloved people have to be in my house, when she has done so many evil things? Can holy sacrifices take away your punishment? When you do evil, you are happy."
The LORD once called you a green olive tree, beautiful with good fruit. But with the roar of a great storm he will set it on fire, and its branches will be broken.
The LORD of Armies, who planted you, has announced disaster against you. For the people of Israel and Judah have done evil and made him angry by burning incense to Baal.
The LORD showed me their plot, so I knew about it. He showed me what they were doing.

I was like a gentle lamb being led to be killed. I did not know they were making plans against me. They said, "Let us destroy the tree and its fruit. Let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."
But you, LORD of Armies, judge fairly. You test the heart and the mind. Let me see you pay them back, for I have placed my case in your hands.
So this is what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth who want to kill you, who say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or we will kill you."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "Look, I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die of hunger.
Not one of them will be left alive. For I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year they are punished."
